text:
Tokyo's most famous food basement sells prawn heads fried to a crunch, but only in the morning, "if at all". Isetan Shinjuku's B1 is full of things that only appear on certain days. Here's what to plan your visit around 👇

🎯 Bet you can't guess which one is sold only three days a month 👉 https://japanbystation.com/isetan-shinjuku-food-hall-what-to-buy

We took our time with this one and checked every price and set day against Isetan's own pages before writing it.

🍤 THE MORNING-ONLY ONE

Tokyo Kitcho fries the heads of kuruma prawns until they crack like crisps. Isetan's own list says they're there in the morning, if at all. Opening is 10:00, so that's when we'd go.

🦐 THE TWICE-A-MONTH ONE

Keito Shindo's "Shurimpo" shrimp crackers appear on just two days a month. Ask at the counter which days are next. A great gift for someone who doesn't like sweets.

🥞 THE THREE-DAYS-A-MONTH ONE

Sasaya Iori, a Kyoto maker founded in 1716, sells its dorayaki as one long roll, only on the 20th, 21st and 22nd. If your Tokyo dates include one of those, put Isetan on that day.

🍮 THE ONLY-HERE ONES

Isetan lists sweets you can't buy anywhere else in 2026: CUSTA custard pudding for ¥432, a Finnish Ekberg cinnamon roll for ¥540, and a lemon cookie box from POMOLOGY for ¥1,944.

🌿 OUR TAKE

Arrive at 10:00, buy lunch downstairs, and eat it on the free rooftop garden on the 7th floor (open to 18:00 in winter).
